issues.legal_issue: A land-tax register correction power cannot be used to change the legal nature of land or effect its conversion.
material_facts: The land was recorded as wetland, while the respondents claimed that it had become dry land.
The respondents sought correction of the Basic Tax Register to change the land classification.
The claimed change in the land’s nature was not an identified clerical or arithmetical error in an order determining tax.
issues.conclusion: The land-tax correction provision could not authorize reclassification or conversion of the land, and the High Court’s direction to correct the register was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18 of the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961 permits rectification of an apparent mistake in an order made under that Act; the correction is confined to errors such as arithmetical or clerical errors in determining tax. A change in the land’s nature over time is not such a mistake. Conversion is governed by the Kerala Land Utilization Order, 1967 or the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act, 2008, as applicable, and a tax register maintained for land-tax purposes cannot bypass those regimes. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.land_reclassification_proceeding: A proceeding was brought seeking to change the recorded classification of land.
predicates.correction_of_tax_register_sought: The applicant asked an authority to change the land classification in a register maintained for land-tax purposes.
predicates.claimed_change_is_substantive_land_conve: The requested change concerned the land’s nature or use rather than an error in calculating tax.

issues.definition: When a proceeding seeks to reclassify land through correction of a land-tax register because of a claimed substantive change in the land’s nature, the register correction cannot itself effect that conversion.

issues.legal_issue: Whether land is paddy land or wetland is determined by its condition and suitability on the ground, not merely by its description in revenue records or deeds.
material_facts: The land was described as wetland in revenue records and in the sale deed, while certificates and the respondents’ claim described it as dry land.
The Court stated that statutory status as paddy land must be determined on the facts as they exist on the ground rather than from the description in records or deeds.
issues.conclusion: The land’s status under the conservation legislation must be assessed from its actual condition on the ground, not solely from its recorded or deed description.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(xii) of the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act, 2008 defines paddy land by reference to land where paddy is cultivated at least once a year or which is suitable for paddy cultivation but is uncultivated and left fallow. The Act’s statutory classification is determined from the facts on the ground, not the description in revenue records or deeds. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.land_status_disputed: The parties disputed whether the land had the characteristics of paddy land or wetland.
predicates.recorded_description_used_to_claim_land_: A party relied on a description in a revenue record or deed to assert the land’s status.

issues.definition: When land status is disputed and a recorded description is relied on, the classification follows the land’s actual condition on the ground.

issues.legal_issue: The conservation legislation governs conversion of land included in the relevant data bank as paddy land or wetland and qualifying as such under the statutory definition.
material_facts: The dispute concerned land whose recorded classification was Nilam, or wetland.
The Court held that land included in the data bank or draft data bank as paddy land or wetland, and qualifying under the statutory definition, is governed by the conservation legislation.
issues.conclusion: Where land is included in the data bank or draft data bank as paddy land or wetland and falls within the statutory definition, conversion is governed by the conservation legislation and its procedures.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(xii) and 2(xviii) of the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act, 2008 define paddy land and wetlands. Section 3 prohibits conversion or reclamation except in accordance with the Act, and Section 13 empowers the District Collector to order reconversion where conversion or reclamation occurred after the Act commenced. Sections 5, 7, 8 and 9 provide for monitoring, reporting and committee functions, including consideration of specified applications. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.land_conversion_proceeding: A proceeding concerns proposed or completed conversion of land to another use.
predicates.land_listed_as_paddy_or_wetland: The land is included in the relevant data bank or draft data bank as paddy land or wetland.
predicates.land_meets_statutory_land_definition: The land has the characteristics of paddy land or wetland under the applicable statutory definition.

issues.definition: A conversion proceeding concerning land that is both listed as paddy land or wetland and meets the statutory definition is governed by the conservation regime.

issues.legal_issue: The land-utilization regime governs conversion of land not included in the relevant data bank and not qualifying as paddy land or wetland under the statutory definition.
material_facts: The Court distinguished land included in the data bank as paddy land or wetland from land not so included.

The Court held that land not included in the data bank and not qualifying as paddy land or wetland under the statutory definition remains governed by the land-utilization regime, even if revenue records describe it as Nilam.
issues.conclusion: Land not included in the data bank and not qualifying as paddy land or wetland under the statutory definition is governed by the Kerala Land Utilization Order, 1967, under which the competent Collector considers a request for other use on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: The Kerala Land Utilization Order, 1967 governs land outside the scope of the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act, 2008. Under Clause 2(a) of the Order, the Collector considers requests for residential use on their merits; the Court also referred to the restrictions and directions in the Government notification of 5 February 2002. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: land_conversion_proceeding and not land_listed_as_paddy_or_wetland and not land_meets_statutory_land_definition

predicates.land_conversion_proceeding: A proceeding concerns proposed or completed conversion of land to another use.
predicates.land_listed_as_paddy_or_wetland: The land is included in the relevant data bank or draft data bank as paddy land or wetland.
predicates.land_meets_statutory_land_definition: The land has the characteristics of paddy land or wetland under the applicable statutory definition.

issues.definition: A conversion proceeding concerning land that is neither listed as paddy land or wetland nor within the statutory definition is governed by the land-utilization regime.

issues.legal_issue: A request to convert land must be considered by the competent authority under the applicable land-conversion regime rather than achieved through a writ directing correction of a land-tax register.
material_facts: The respondents sought a writ directing correction of the Basic Tax Register and reclassification of the land.
They had not first applied to a competent authority for conversion under the applicable statutory regime.

The Court directed the respondents to approach the competent authorities, which were to consider their applications under the relevant legislation and the 2002 notification, on the facts and supporting material presented.
issues.conclusion: The respondents had to apply to the competent authorities under the applicable regime, and those authorities were to decide the applications in accordance with the relevant law and the material submitted.
issues.legal_principle: The competent authorities under the Kerala Land Utilization Order, 1967 or the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act, 2008, as applicable, determine conversion requests. A direction to alter the Basic Tax Register cannot substitute for the statutory inquiry and procedure. Applications are to be considered under the relevant statutory provisions and the Government notification of 5 February 2002. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.land_conversion_proceeding: A proceeding concerns a request to convert land to another use.
predicates.conversion_application_not_made_to_compe: The person seeking conversion has not applied to the authority empowered to decide conversion under the applicable regime.
predicates.writ_seeks_tax_register_change_to_effect: The applicant seeks a court direction to change a land-tax register as a means of achieving conversion.

issues.definition: When a conversion request has not been placed before the competent authority and a writ seeks to achieve it through a tax-register change, the conversion request must be decided by the competent authority.
